# Requirements Quality Checklist: Azure Roster Persistence

**Purpose**: Review the Azure-only persistence requirements for completeness, clarity, consistency, measurable acceptance, and implementation readiness.
**Created**: 2026-11-17
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are the responsibilities of the Azure-persistent and local in-memory storage modes explicitly defined without leaving a third storage mode implied? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002–FR-007]
- [ ] CHK002 Does the specification define the complete lifecycle of persisted roster data, including creation, loading, restart, redeployment, scale-out, and unavailable-database behavior? [Completeness, Spec §User Story 1, §FR-004–FR-005]
- [ ] CHK003 Are all five roster fields, their existing validation rules, and their treatment in both storage modes identified as in-scope? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK004 Are the required configuration inputs and provisioning responsibilities for MySQL In App sufficiently described for implementation, including who supplies and maintains them? [Gap, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK005 Does the specification define whether the existing JSON feed must reflect persisted Azure data and local in-memory data consistently? [Completeness, Spec §Assumptions]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK006 Is “running in the Azure deployment environment” defined with an unambiguous hosting-environment signal rather than inferred only from the presence of configuration values? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002, §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK007 Is “database is available” defined in terms that distinguish valid configuration, reachable database, usable schema, and successful read/write operations? [Clarity, Spec §User Story 1, §Key Entities]
- [ ] CHK008 Are “understandable error,” “actionable retry message,” and “where possible” sufficiently specific to establish the required user-visible behavior? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-010, §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK009 Is the ordering of multiple roster entries explicitly defined as a deterministic rule that applies identically to both storage modes? [Gap, Spec §User Story 3]
- [ ] CHK010 Is duplicate-entry behavior stated precisely enough to distinguish preservation of duplicates from accidental deduplication? [Clarity, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK011 Is the boundary between Azure-managed configuration and application source/configuration clear enough to prevent credentials from being committed, logged, or returned in errors? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK012 Do the Azure-only selection requirement and the requirement to avoid database access locally remain consistent when local configuration contains Azure-looking connection values? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002, §FR-006, §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK013 Do the requirements consistently prohibit silent in-memory fallback after an Azure persistence failure while still allowing the existing in-memory implementation in local mode? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006, §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK014 Are the restart-loss expectations for local entries and restart-retention expectations for Azure entries explicitly separated so they cannot be interpreted as conflicting behavior? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005, §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK015 Do the success criteria and acceptance scenarios use the same definition of a successful submission and the same treatment of failed persistence? [Consistency, Spec §User Stories 1–3, §Success Criteria]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK016 Can each Azure acceptance scenario be evaluated objectively for saved-before-success, visibility after restart, and failure reporting without relying on subjective judgment? [Measurability, Spec §User Story 1]
- [ ] CHK017 Does the two-second Index-page target define the relevant normal operating conditions, data shape, and whether the measurement includes database connection or schema initialization? [Clarity, Spec §SC-005]
- [ ] CHK018 Are the “100%” success criteria scoped to a defined test environment, sample size, and failure classification so they are meaningful and reproducible? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001–SC-003]
- [ ] CHK019 Does the specification define objective evidence for confirming that local execution did not contact the Azure database? [Gap, Spec §SC-002, §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK020 Does the specification define objective evidence that a failed Azure submission was not reported as saved and that the entered values were preserved for retry? [Measurability, Spec §FR-009–FR-010, §SC-003]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK021 Are first-run Azure behavior, an empty Azure roster, an existing Azure roster, and repeated page loads all covered as distinct user or system scenarios? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 1, §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK022 Are local execution, Visual Studio execution, local restart, and local configuration containing Azure-looking values each covered independently? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 2, §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK023 Are valid and invalid submissions compared across both storage modes with requirements for identical validation and field display behavior? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 3]
- [ ] CHK024 Are concurrent submissions or multiple application instances addressed for ordering, duplicate preservation, and consistency when Azure is scaled out? [Gap, Spec §User Story 1, §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK025 Does the specification define expected behavior for reads that fail after previously saved Azure entries exist? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases, §Key Entities]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK026 Are missing, malformed, incomplete, and unreachable Azure connection settings distinguished, with a defined outcome for each? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases, §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK027 Are database schema absence, schema incompatibility, and migration/provisioning failure covered separately from ordinary database unavailability? [Gap, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK028 Are transient failures and retry behavior bounded clearly enough to avoid duplicate writes or indefinite request delays? [Clarity, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK029 Are empty fields, boundary-length values, special characters, and duplicate roster submissions covered by the existing validation and persistence requirements? [Coverage, Spec §FR-001, §FR-008, §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK030 Is the behavior defined when storage mode changes between application executions, including explicit confirmation that local entries are not migrated to Azure? [Clarity, Spec §Edge Cases]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK031 Are performance requirements stated for asynchronous persistence, bounded reads, connection management, and avoidance of repeated database reads within a request? [Completeness, Plan §Technical Context]
- [ ] CHK032 Are security requirements sufficient to cover parameterized database operations, secret redaction in logs and errors, and least exposure of connection details? [Completeness, Spec §FR-011, Constitution §V]
- [ ] CHK033 Are accessibility requirements for validation, persistence errors, retry guidance, keyboard access, and preserved form values explicitly applicable to the new failure states? [Coverage, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK034 Are observability requirements defined for diagnosing Azure persistence failures without exposing credentials or connection-string secrets? [Gap, Spec §FR-010–FR-011, Constitution §V]
- [ ] CHK035 Is the opt-in nature and required configuration of real MySQL integration tests documented well enough to prevent accidental dependency on Azure resources in ordinary local test runs? [Clarity, Plan §Technical Context]

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [ ] CHK036 Are the required MySQL provider, MySQL In App availability, Azure App Service configuration, and database lifecycle dependencies identified with ownership or validation responsibility? [Completeness, Plan §Technical Context, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK037 Is the relationship between the Azure connection-string variable and the provider-specific connection-string syntax specified sufficiently to preserve every required value, including the generated port? [Clarity, Plan §Summary, §Technical Context]
- [ ] CHK038 Does the specification explicitly identify the consequences if the generated port is missing, invalid, or replaced by an implicit default? [Coverage, Plan §Constraints]
- [ ] CHK039 Are schema creation, migration, deployment timing, and idempotency requirements defined rather than deferred entirely to implementation planning? [Gap, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK040 Are the assumptions about the existing roster contract, Index page, JSON feed, and duplicate behavior validated against the current application scope? [Dependency, Spec §Assumptions]

## Ambiguities and Conflicts

- [ ] CHK041 Does the specification resolve whether a failed Azure read should show an empty roster, retain a prior snapshot, or display an error, avoiding a misleading empty-state result? [Ambiguity, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK042 Does the specification resolve whether database initialization is performed at startup, lazily on first use, or through deployment provisioning, and what users see if initialization has not completed? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-005, §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK043 Does the specification define whether a successful write must be followed by a fresh read or whether the submitted entry may be added to the current page state? [Gap, Spec §FR-004–FR-005]
- [ ] CHK044 Are failure, retry, and validation messages required to remain consistent with existing Index-page terminology and accessibility patterns? [Consistency, Spec §FR-010, §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK045 Are all requirements needed for scale-out consistency and duplicate handling explicit enough to avoid provider- or implementation-specific interpretations? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-005, §Edge Cases]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`.
- This checklist evaluates the written requirements; it does not verify implementation behavior.
